rationale: The expected file output/replication/table6.csv was not written, but the run produced the equivalent evidence in /workspace/output/replication/codebase/outputs/table6.json (step 4, port_table6.R, exit 0). The EDUC coefficients there are col1 OLS 0.05734, col2 TSLS 0.05530, col3 OLS 0.05735, col4 TSLS 0.09480, col5 OLS 0.05205, col6 TSLS 0.03927, col7 OLS 0.05206, col8 TSLS 0.07788, at N=486926 (men born 1940-1949, 1980 Census) — matching the reported N exactly. Rounded to 4 decimals these are [0.0573, 0.0553, 0.0573, 0.0948, 0.0520, 0.0393, 0.0521, 0.0779], identical to the paper's Table VI values with <0.2% relative error on every cell. The qualitative claims also hold: OLS estimates cluster at 0.052-0.057; the quadratic-age TSLS columns (col4 0.0948, col8 0.0779) are higher than their no-age-control counterparts (col2 0.0553, col6 0.0393), confirming the simple Wald is biased downward while TSLS with quadratic age is positive and significant (col4 t=4.26, col8 t=3.26). No relevant fix appears in fix_severity.json. All eight cells within 5% → match.
